evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: most of our customers have two concerns when they're booking a move. One, being that they movers are not gonna arrive on time or two, damage to their items, or any of those are concern for you.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised budget/time concerns ('milked', overtime, flat fee preference). Rep acknowledged ('Absolutely! And I do apologize that happened to you') and pivoted to damage and time guarantees without asking clarifying follow-up like 'tell me more about that' before moving to solutions.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Saturday December 19th is not identified as Best Value or not. Rep states '$222 and that's for two movers and 126 foot box truck' for that specific day but does not offer an alternative cheaper day or ask about date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep says 'And then there is no deposit required to get on our schedule and then there's no fees to change or cancel as well' (rate lock/no deposit), then customer immediately says 'Well let's go ahead and do it then' — the ask was never explicitly made; customer volunteered to book before being asked 'Would you like our help with your move?'

top_strength: Brianne delivered both promises (On-Time Guarantee with specific discount structure and $2,000 No Worries Damage Coverage) in full, recognizable form, directly addressing Jordan's core concerns about prior bad experiences.
coaching_note: Step 5 is missing the pricing contrast (competitors' hourly model vs. your all-inclusive model) — you stated the hourly rate but didn't frame why Einstein's model is different — and Step 7 never included an explicit ask for the business; the customer volunteered to book, which left no moment to confirm they understood the rate lock before they said yes.
